newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq paper complains about Turkish incursion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq paper complains about Turkish incursion.

text.p: The newspaper of Iraq's ruling Baath party complained on Monday about the presence of Turkish troops in northern Iraq, saying Ankara should reconsider its policy.

"Campaigns of condemnation and denunciation, albeit significant, are not enough. What is needed is that these campaigns turn into an organised international move to pressure Turkey to withdraw its troops," al-Thawra said in a commentary.

"Turkey has crossed the red line in good neighbourly relations and the Turkish government must reconsider this policy which does not serve the future of security and stability in the region," the paper said.

It said while the world was unanimous in condemning the latest sweep by Turkish troops of northern Iraq, the United States was trying to justify their presence in the area under the pretext of hunting down rebels of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
Several thousand Turkish troops backed by tanks and heavy artillery have pushed into northern Iraq since Wednesday in a foray against PKK elements hiding in the mountainous region.
Iraq has officially denounced the attack and asked for an immediate withdrawl of the troops but has so far stopped short of calling on the U.N. Security Council to convene and condemn the operation.
